verdict.line: You lose short trades and all-ins from levels 3-6 when Irelia strings Flawless Duet into Bladesurge, but you win the game once Stridebreaker and Mortal Reminder come online, backed by a 53.3% win rate over 557 games.

brief.thesis: Irelia holds lane and solo-kill advantage because Bladesurge (Q) gives her a repeatable dash-and-heal gap closer on a 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown that resets on marked or killed targets, and Flawless Duet (E) adds a stun before she commits Vanguard's Edge (R). Nothing in your kit closes that gap safely before level 6, so contested trades favor her early. But Garen's execute threat and itemized tankiness let him take over once both champions finish their spikes, which is why the head-to-head win rate sits at 53.3% over 557 games despite the lane itself playing defensive for you.

theirWindow.what: Flawless Duet's two blades converge and stun plus Mark anyone caught between them, opening a follow-up Bladesurge or Vanguard's Edge combo. Don't stand between the blade paths during a trade, and if you get caught, disengage rather than fight through it.

yourWindow.what: With no gap closer up she can't dash in or reset off a last hit, so step forward and spin Judgment for free damage. This is your best window to push a short skirmish or force a trade she can't escape.

start.why: The extra sustain against her Bladesurge pokes and auto trades wins out at 52.9% over 291 games, matching the defensive shape of this lane.

boots.why: Highest win rate of the two options at 59.5% over 437 games; the attack speed lets you land more Perseverance-friendly short trades and spin Judgment more often per fight.

core.why: Core of the top win-rate path (63.6% over 121 games); the slow-on-hit lets you actually stick to Irelia once her Bladesurge is down.
Attack speed spike that turns your Judgment and auto-attack trades into real DPS during the levels where you're supposed to be even or ahead.
Grievous Wounds directly cuts the healing Irelia gets back from every Bladesurge cast, removing her main sustain tool in extended fights.

situational.when: she is snowballing off Bladesurge heals and you need grievous wounds online before Mortal Reminder finishes
you need more health and stickiness to survive extended skirmishes into her damage
you're ahead and want more burst and mobility to force kills once your R is up

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's healing scales with extended trades, directly offsetting Irelia's own Bladesurge sustain and rewarding the slower, patient fight pattern this matchup demands.

summoners.why: The dominant pick at 56.1% win rate over 96.1% of games; Ignite cuts through the healing she gets back from Bladesurge and secures kills your execute can't quite finish.

playing.title: Punish when Bladesurge is down
playing.detail: Without her Q up, Irelia has no gap closer or escape. Step forward and spin Judgment freely; your E cooldown drops to 10s and then 9s as you rank it, so you can trade more often than she can answer.

playing.title: Don't stand between her blades
playing.detail: Flawless Duet only stuns and Marks targets caught between the two converging blades. Sidestep the lane center when she telegraphs it rather than walking through it during a trade.

playing.title: Use Decisive Strike to disengage, not engage
playing.detail: If you get hit by her E stun, your Q's move speed burst and slow removal are for escaping the follow-up combo, not chasing. Reset and let Perseverance heal you back up.

playing.title: Avoid short, repeated pokes
playing.detail: Perseverance only kicks in when you haven't been hit recently. Take one clean E-plus-auto exchange, then back off and let the passive regen close the gap instead of trading again immediately.

playing.title: Hold R for a clean execute
playing.detail: Demacian Justice only threatens at 400 range, so don't flash it in. Wait until she's already engaged or overextended, since her own R has a long 125-85s cooldown at early ranks and won't be up to punish you back.

playing.title: Build toward Mortal Reminder on schedule
playing.detail: Every Bladesurge cast heals her, so the Grievous Wounds from Mortal Reminder in your core path is not optional. Rush it if she's snowballing off repeated dashes onto minions or you.

playing.title: Don't shove into her all-in window
playing.detail: Pushing the wave hard between levels 3 and 6 just gives her a marked minion to reset Bladesurge off, closing the gap for free. Let her come to your minions instead.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, rune pages, summoner spells, and every win rate above are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch (16.18.1); the timing windows and trade-pattern reasoning are my own read of the kit interactions.

stats.opponentTip: Keep an eye out on Irelia’s (P) stacks and her Conqueror stacks when engaging combat. If you got hit with her (E) stun, use [Q]-[W] to retreat.
